rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception completes the warning by dividing people into two groups: those who incur loss and those who escape it.
rows.anchor: فيتقرر الحكم تاماً في نفس السامع مبيناً أن الناس فريقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good avoid loss so long as they do not omit good acts by committing their opposites, sins.
rows.anchor: لا يلحقهم الخسران بحال إذا لم يتركوا شيئاً من الصالحات بارتكاب أضدادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is among the greatest good deeds: a believer who avoids sins or repents of them gains the recompensed profit of a good outcome; one who neither does good nor repents remains in loss.
rows.anchor: ومن أكبر الأعمال الصالحات التوبة من الذنوب لمقترفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss ranges from eternal loss caused by denying God's oneness and the Messenger's truth to lesser degrees measured by outward and inward sins; minor lapses may be forgiven when major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: فأعظمه وخالده الخسر المنجر عن انتفاء الإيمان بوحدانية الله وصدق الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns the future, especially the eternal afterlife, and should not be judged by worldly turns of fortune.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخبر مراد به الحصول في المستقبل بقرينة مقام الإنذار والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form of loss may indicate kinds of loss, or magnification and comprehensiveness in the oath's threatening context.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { خسر } يجوز أن يكون للتنويع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses the people in great loss as the polytheists.
rows.anchor: إن الناس لفي خسران عظيم وهم المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural means the whole class of good deeds, comprehensively including all religiously commanded good acts and abstention from sins.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس مراد به الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause and its coordination hint at why these people are excepted: faith and good deeds are the opposite of the loss predicated of everyone else.
rows.anchor: مضمون الصلة ومعطوفها إيماء إلى علة حكم الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith applies uniformly to its particulars, while good deeds admit degrees; accordingly, freedom from encompassing loss varies with the amount of good done.
rows.anchor: وأما الصالحات فعمومها مقول عليه بالتشكك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception implies that the rest of humanity loses through lacking faith and good action; the relative clause identifies faith and good action as preventing loss from engulfing a person.
rows.anchor: سبب كون بقية الإنسان في خسر هو عدم الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhorting one another to truth is singled out from good deeds for emphasis, since people may wrongly think righteous action benefits only oneself.
rows.anchor: عطف الخاص على العام للاهتمام به لأنه قد يغفل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in truth includes teaching guidance and sound beliefs, and training oneself to understand them by doing good and avoiding wrong.
rows.anchor: تعليم حقائق الهدى وعقائد الصواب وإراضة النفس على فهمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is also singled out as a particular of good deeds, specifically the endurance required to establish truth and bear harm in doing so.
rows.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر عطف على التواصي بالحق عطف الخاص على العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is restraining oneself from a desired thing or its pursuit, either to avoid resulting harm or to gain a benefit; examples include jihad, pilgrimage, and arduous work for reward, wealth, or reputation.
rows.anchor: منع المرء نفسه من تحصيل ما يشتهيه أو من محاولة تحصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience includes enduring the displeasure or verbal abuse one may face when enjoining what is right.
rows.anchor: ومن الصبر الصبر على ما يلاقيه المسلم إذا أمر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enduring the effort involved in sinful pleasures is not patience, because desire for that effort outweighs aversion to the effort of leaving the sin.
rows.anchor: فليس من الصبر لأن ذلك التحمل منبعث عن رجحان اشتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two exhortations encompass the religious good: Islamic beliefs and ethics fall under truth, while good works and avoiding sins fall under patience.
rows.anchor: العقائد الإسلامية والأخلاق الدينية مندرجة في الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience underpins the virtues: moral discipline requires resisting many desires until good character becomes a settled trait.
rows.anchor: التخلق بالصبر ملاك فضائل الأخلاق كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur cites ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs's couplet to illustrate giving up beloved food and restraining a wayward heart to avoid lasting disgrace.
rows.anchor: إذا المرء لم يترك طعاماً يحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited hadith says Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires, supporting the need for self-restraint in righteous action.
rows.anchor: حفت الجنة بالمكاره وحفت النار بالشهوات

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is quoted as saying that patience is a mount that never stumbles.
rows.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب : « الصبر مطية لا تكبو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers to his fuller discussion of patience under the command to seek help through patience and prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى الكلام على الصبر مشبعاً عند قوله تعالى : { استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form makes mutual exhortation to truth and patience a constant feature of believers' communal life; it presumes that people practice what they urge others to maintain.
rows.anchor: وأفادت صيغة التواصي بالحق وبالصبر أن يكون شأن حياة المؤمنين قائماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal exhortation suggests believers will uphold truth and endure hardship for the interests of Islam and its community, since exhorters ordinarily regard the matter as worth maintaining.
rows.anchor: أن أحداً لا يوصي غيره بملازمة أمر إلا وهو يرى ذلك الأمر خليقاً بالملازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assumption that exhorters practice what they urge recalls God's rebuke to Israelites who command goodness while neglecting themselves.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى توبيخاً لبني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this point to the earlier discussion of people failing to urge one another to feed the needy.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم هذا المعنى عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial fa explicitly makes the following statement a consequence of, and connected to, the preceding discourse.
rows.anchor: موقع الفاء صريح في اتصال ما بعدها بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the whole sura is Meccan, the worshipers are the same class as those who deny judgment, repel the orphan, and fail to urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالمصلين عين المراد بالذي يكذب بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them worshipers replaces a pronoun with another listed trait, avoiding a monotonous run of six parallel traits; placing woe here shows all their traits occasion it, as al-Kashshaf hints.
rows.anchor: إظهار في مقام الإضمار كأنه قيل : فويل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Meccan reading, calling them worshipers is mockery: it means people who do not pray and are not Muslims, confirmed by the next description.
rows.anchor: فوصفهم ب« المصلين » إذن تهكم

rows.speaker: ابن وهب وأشهب عن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ashhab transmit from Malik the view that if the sura, or these verses, are Medinan, the inattentive worshipers are hypocrites; the fa links this passage to what precedes.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا ابن وهب وأشهب عن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural suits the apparent reading that the denier is a class; if an earlier view meant one specific person, the plural generalizes to include him among others with these traits.
rows.anchor: وجيء في هذه الصفة بصيغة الجمع لأن المراد ب { الذي يكذب بالدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause restricts the woe to worshipers inattentive to their prayer, not worshipers generally, and further reinforces the mockery.
rows.anchor: صفة { للمصلين } مقيِّدة لحكم الموصوف فإن الويل للمصلي الساهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ʿan with inattentive means they have gone beyond establishing prayer and abandoned it; the verse is unrelated to the legal rules for mistakes within prayer.
rows.anchor: وعدي { ساهون } بحرف { عن } لإفادة أنهم تجاوزوا إقامة صلاتهم وتركوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible meaning is people who pray only for show and abandon prayer when alone.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يؤدون الصلاة إلاّ رياء فإذا خلوا تركوا الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible meaning is people who pray without intention or sincerity, seeming heedless while praying; calling them heedless is mockery.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معناه : الذين يصلون دون نية وإخلاص فهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects this insincere prayer to the hypocrites described as showing off and remembering God only a little.
rows.anchor: { يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلاً في المنافقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They intend people to see an apparently good state that is false, so people will praise qualities they do not possess.
rows.anchor: و ( يراءون ) يقصدون أن يرى الناس أنهم على حال حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb occurs in the reciprocal form; no simple form is attested, since the act entails repeated display.
rows.anchor: وارد في الكلام على صيغة المفاعلة ولم يسمع منه فعل مجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿun can mean financial assistance: they withhold their surplus or charity from the poor; charity in early Islam was obligatory in an unspecified form before zakat was legislated.
rows.anchor: و{ الماعون } :  يطلق على الإعانة بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that unspecified charity was obligatory in the early Islamic period before zakat was instituted.
rows.anchor: كانت الصدقة واجبة في صدر الإسلام بغير تعيين قبل مشروعية الزكاة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وابن شهاب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Ibn Shihab say al-maʿun means wealth in Quraysh usage.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب وابن شهاب : الماعون : المال بلسان قريش

rows.speaker: أشهب عن مالك
rows.claim: Ashhab reports from Malik that al-maʿun means zakat.
rows.anchor: وروى أشهب عن مالك : الماعون : الزكاة

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: The poet al-Raʿi's line pairs withholding al-maʿun with neglecting tahleel; Ibn ʿAshur reads tahleel as prayer and the line as evidence that al-maʿun means zakat.
rows.anchor:
ويشهد له قول الراعي :
قوم على الإسلام لمّا يمنعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿun can also mean household implements such as vessels and tools for cooking, fastening, or digging, which cost the owner nothing to lend or give.
rows.anchor: ويطلق على ما يستعان به على عمل البيت من آنية وآلات طبخ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿA'isha says al-maʿun means water, fire, and salt.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة : الماعون الماء والنار والملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These interpretations condemn extreme stinginess: withholding even something whose lending does not harm its owner.
rows.anchor: وهذا ذم لهم بمنتهى البخل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the subject pronoun before the verbal predicate strengthens and emphasizes the assertion.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Medinan view, these are hypocrites; calling them worshipers means they outwardly present themselves as praying, as in the verse about hypocrites appearing to fear a sura's revelation.
rows.anchor: فإطلاق المصلين عليهم بمعنى المتظاهرين بأنهم يصلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-maʿun means charity or zakat; the author compares the hypocrites' withholding to their clasping their hands.
rows.anchor: { ويمنعون الماعون } أي الصدقة أو الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa of consequence connects these traits: those who outwardly pray but privately abandon prayer belong among the deniers who repel orphans and fail to urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: كان مفاد فاء التفريع أن أولئك المتظاهرين بالصلاة

rows.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
rows.claim: Hibat Allah ibn Salama reports in al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh that these three verses were revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.
rows.anchor: وحكى هبة الله بن سلامة في كتاب « الناسخ والمنسوخ »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the report that the verses concern one man, the plural refers to a singular, as in the statement that Noah's people denied the messengers, meaning their messenger.
rows.anchor: فإطلاق صيغة الجمع عليه مراد بها واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahw literally means losing awareness of something previously known; here it is a mocking metaphor for deliberate turning away and abandonment.
rows.anchor: والسهو حقيقته :  الذهول عن أمر سبق علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor resembles saying that people forget their false gods, where forget means turn away from them.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله تعالى : { وتنسون ما تشركون } [ الأنعام : 41 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also compares metaphorical heedlessness with turning away from God's signs, in two other verses.
rows.anchor: ومثله استعارة الغفلة للإعراض في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is not for genuine forgetfulness in prayer, since forgetfulness is lifted from this community; the description instead mocks people called worshipers who do not pray.
rows.anchor: وليس المقصود الوعيد على السهو الحقيقي عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling on real forgetfulness confirms the mockery: their label as worshipers describes people who in fact do not pray.
rows.anchor: وذلك ينادي على أن وصفهم بالمصلين تهكم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author proposes a general principle: when revelation is attached to an earlier passage, its wording is shaped to fit that context, which explains the consequential fa.
rows.anchor: إذا أراد الله إنزال شيء من القرآن ملحقاً بشيء قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Qur'an codices, al-Tirmidhi's Jamiʿ, and most tafsir works call the sura Surat Tabbat, after its opening word.
rows.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في أكثر المصاحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some codices and tafsirs name it Surat al-Masad; al-Itqan mentions only this and Surat Tabbat.
rows.anchor: وسميت في بعض المصاحف وفي بعض التفاسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A number of exegetes call it Surat Abi Lahab, understood as the sura mentioning Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: وسماها جمع من المفسرين { سورة أبي لهب }

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan titles it Surat al-Lahab; Ibn ʿAshur says he has not seen this title elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وعنونها أبو حيان في تفسيره { سورة اللهب } ولم أره لغيره

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi titled it Sura of what came from Abu Lahab; Ibn ʿAshur treats that as a descriptive heading, not a name.
rows.anchor: وعنونها ابن العربي في أحكام القرآن سورة ما كان من أبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus and is counted as the sixth sura revealed, after al-Fatiha and before al-Takwir.
rows.anchor:
وهي مكية بالاتفاق .
وعدت السادسة من السور نزولاً ، نزلت بعد سورة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report dates the sura's revelation to the fourth year of the Prophet's mission.
rows.anchor: روي أن نزولها كان في السنة الرابعة من البعثة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the two Sahihs, Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Prophet called Quraysh together on Safa with a warning call, said they would believe his warning about an imminent enemy, and Abu Lahab cursed him and asked if that was why he gathered them; the sura then came down.
rows.anchor: على ما في الصحيحين عن ابن عباس قال  صعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم على الصفا فنادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya sabahah is a call used to warn people of an enemy approaching in the morning.
rows.anchor: كلمة ينادى بها للإنذار من عدو يصبح القوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report in the two Sahihs, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas, links the Safa incident to the command to warn the closest kindred.
rows.anchor: في الصحيحين من رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse in Surat al-Shuʿara was revealed later, Ibn ʿAshur resolves the report by positing an earlier, similar warning verse before Surat Tabbat.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن آية { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } من سورة الشعراء وهي متأخرة النزول

rows.speaker: أبو أسامة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Usama's report reaching Ibn ʿAbbas gives an earlier wording, adding 'and your people, the sincere among them'; Ibn ʿAshur takes it as the similar pre-sura command.
rows.anchor: أبو أسامة يبلغ ابن عباس لما نزلت { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura rebukes and threatens Abu Lahab for his insult, and threatens his wife for supporting him and hating the Prophet.
rows.anchor: زجر أبي لهب على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with destruction signals the sura's reproach and threat, a fitting opening for a satire, like a poem that begins by cursing its target.
rows.anchor: افتتاح السورة بالتبات مشعر بأنها نزلت لتوبيخ ووعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening resembles the threat opening Surat al-Mutaffifin with the word woe.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى :  { ويل للمطففين }

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن الحكم
rows.claim: The opening line by ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam curses Qays for abandoning the Muslims' borders and turning away, illustrating a satiric opening of denunciation.
rows.anchor: قول عبد الرحمان بن الحكم من شعراء « الحماسة »

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: Abu Tammam begins a satire with fire, disgrace, harm, and destruction, another opening that forecasts denunciation.
rows.anchor: قول أبي تمام في طالعة هجاء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الخازن
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn al-Khazin adapted that kind of forecast in the opening of a congratulatory poem on a birth.
rows.anchor: أخذ أبو بكر بن الخازن قوله في طالع قصيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabb means loss and destruction; the wording is both a prayer and a rebuke, returning Abu Lahab's own insult against Muhammad as fitting recompense.
rows.anchor: والكلام دعاء وتقريع لأبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unassigned report says Abu Lahab took a stone to throw at the Prophet after insulting him; this explains why the curse names his hands.
rows.anchor: لما روي من أن أبا لهب لما قال للنبيء : « تباً لك سائر اليوم

rows.speaker: طارق المحاربي
rows.claim: Tariq al-Muharibi reports seeing Abu Lahab pursue Muhammad at Dhu al-Majaz, bloodying his legs while calling him a liar and warning people not to believe him.
rows.anchor: وروي عن طارق المحاربي قال : « بينا أنا بسوق ذي المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands are named because they caused the Prophet's harm; this resembles a curse wishing stones in the mouth of someone who says something offensive.
rows.anchor: فوقع الدعاء على يديه لأنهما سبب أذى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse invokes God's curse on the hands of people who withhold hospitality, illustrating a curse directed at hands as agents of action.
rows.anchor: قول النابغة : قعود الذي أبياتهم يثمدونهم

rows.speaker: أعرابي من بني أسد
rows.claim: An Asadi Bedouin's verse blesses Maswar's hands because they answered a call for aid, showing the opposite use of hands as instruments of help.
rows.anchor: وقال أعرابي من بني أسد : دعوت لما نابني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab was ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle, and was also known as Abu ʿUtba after his son.
rows.anchor: وأبو لهب : هو عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب وهو عم النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation says he was called Abu Lahab in pre-Islamic times for his handsome, radiant face; Tariq's report and a similar report from Rabiʿa ibn ʿAbbad al-Dayli indicate the nickname was well known.
rows.anchor: فقيل :  كان يكنى بذلك في الجاهلية ( لحسنه وإشراق وجهه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an may use his kunya instead of ʿAbd al-ʿUzza because that personal name invokes worship of al-ʿUzza, which the Qur'an does not endorse.
rows.anchor: فسماه القرآن بكنيته دون اسمه لأن في اسمه عبادة العزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he was better known by his kunya than by his personal name.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya also permits a pointed implication that he belongs to Hell, since lahab is the flame of a fire once its smoke has dissipated.
rows.anchor: أو لأن في كنيته ما يتأتى به التوجيه بكونه صائراً إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ab can denote someone devoted to or associated with what follows; the author uses familiar kunyas and Taftazani's account of names as omens to explain the suggestive Abu Lahab epithet.
rows.anchor: والأبُ :  يطلق على ملازم ما أضيف إليه

rows.speaker: التفتزاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftazani's discussion of proper names and auspicious naming is cited to explain the kunya's implied association with Hell.
rows.anchor: كما أشار إليه التفتزاني في مبحث العَلَمِيَّة من « شرح المفتاح »

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poet jokes that Abu al-Mahasin has no son among his children, illustrating how a person's name can suggest an outcome that is not borne out literally.
rows.anchor:
وأنشد قول الشاعر :
قصدت أبا المحاسن كي أراه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Lahab's daughter told the Prophet that people called her the daughter of the firewood of Hell, suggesting another possible sense of her father's kunya.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce lahab with a fatha; Ibn Kathir reads the h with sukun, a dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور لفظ { لهب } بفتح الهاء ، وقرأه ابن كثير بسكون الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sukun may reflect the common Arabic tendency to suppress a vowel on a medial consonant after an initial consonant with a vowel.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كثيراً ما يسكنون عين الكلمة المتحركة مع الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronunciation may result from changing a vowel when a common noun becomes a proper name.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون ذلك لأن { لهب } صار جزءَ عَلَم والعرب قد يغيرون بعض حركات الاسم

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح بن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the altered vowel in Shums as a proper-name change, like Maʿdi Yakrib, Tahluk, and Mawhab.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جنيّ في كتاب « إعراب الحماسة »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Salma, Zuhayr's father's kunya, similarly has a changed vowel because Salma, originally a feminine name, was transferred to a man's name.
rows.anchor: وكما قالوا : أبو سلمى بضم السين كنية والد زهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir does not apply the sukun in Abu Lahab's proper name to the phrase dhati lahab; Ibn ʿAshur suggests Meccans knew the kunya's settled pronunciation through frequent use.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لم يسكن ابن كثير الهاء من قوله تعالى :  { ذات لهب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause may coordinate a curse on Abu Lahab himself with the prior curse on his hands, intensifying the rebuke; the whole and part meanings justify coordination.
rows.anchor: إما معطوفة على جملة :  { تبت يدا أبي لهب } عطف الدعاء على الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the clauses differ as whole and part, their semantic difference licenses the conjunction; verbal emphasis would not be conjoined with waw, as discussed in Surat al-Kafirun.
rows.anchor: وتفيد بذلك تأكيداً لجملة :  { تبت يدا أبي لهب } لأنها بمعناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the second clause is circumstantial with waw al-hal, not a prayer, but confirmation that the destruction invoked has occurred; the preceding line is then ridicule or a wish for more destruction.
rows.anchor: والواو واوَ الحال ولا تكون دعاءً إنما هي تحقيق لحصول ما دعي عليه به

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's line says that God did indeed repay ʿAdi with the stated punishment, illustrating a circumstantial clause that confirms a fulfilled outcome.
rows.anchor: كقول النابغة :  جزى ربه عني عدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading adds qad before tabb, supporting the circumstantial analysis and making the preceding words a taunt rather than a request for destruction.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا الوجه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود « وقد تب »

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
rows.claim: Ibn Rawaha's poem about his martyrdom at Mu'ta uses a prayer for guidance followed by confirmation that he was indeed guided, illustrating the circumstantial reading.
rows.anchor: كقول عبد الله بن رواحة حين خروجه إلى غزوة مؤتة
